rules.name: TODO Security Comment
rules.description: A TODO/FIXME comment mentions security or authentication, indicating an unresolved security issue.
rules.fix_suggestion: Resolve the security TODO before shipping to production. Create a tracked issue if the fix is non-trivial.

rules.name: Hardcoded IP Address
rules.description: A hardcoded IP address is embedded in source code. This can expose internal infrastructure topology and makes configuration inflexible.
rules.fix_suggestion: Move hardcoded IP addresses to configuration files or environment variables so they can be changed without code modifications.

rules.name: Disabled SSL/TLS Verification
rules.description: SSL/TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled, making the connection vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.
rules.fix_suggestion: Always verify SSL certificates in production. Pass verify=True (the default) or supply a CA bundle path to requests.

rules.name: Debug Mode Enabled
rules.description: Debug mode is enabled in production code, potentially exposing stack traces, internal paths, and sensitive configuration.
rules.fix_suggestion: Set debug=False in production. Use environment variables to control debug mode: debug=os.getenv('DEBUG','false').lower()=='true'.

rules.name: Weak Random for Security
rules.description: The random module is not cryptographically secure and must not be used for security-sensitive operations like tokens, passwords, or session IDs.
rules.fix_suggestion: Use the secrets module for security-sensitive randomness: secrets.token_hex(), secrets.choice(), secrets.randbelow().

rules.name: Insecure HTTP URL
rules.description: An HTTP (non-HTTPS) URL is used. Data transmitted over HTTP is unencrypted and susceptible to interception.
rules.fix_suggestion: Use HTTPS URLs for all external connections. Update http:// to https://.

rules.name: console.log of Sensitive Data (JS)
rules.description: Logging potentially sensitive data (password, token, secret) to the console can expose credentials in browser developer tools or server logs.
rules.fix_suggestion: Remove console.log statements containing sensitive data before deploying to production.

rules.name: Overly Permissive CORS (ALL Origins)
rules.description: CORS is configured to allow all origins (*). This disables same-origin protection and may expose APIs to unauthorized cross-origin requests.
rules.fix_suggestion: Restrict CORS to specific trusted origins. Use an allowlist instead of wildcard: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://yourdomain.com.

rules.name: Sensitive Data in URL Parameter
rules.description: Passwords, tokens, or API keys passed as URL query parameters are logged in server access logs, browser history, and Referer headers.
rules.fix_suggestion: Pass sensitive values in HTTP headers or the request body, never in URL query parameters.

rules.name: PHP Short Open Tags
rules.description: PHP short open tags (<?) may not be supported on all servers and can cause parse errors or security issues when configurations differ.
rules.fix_suggestion: Use the full <?php opening tag for portability and security.
